qualitative.gate_2_reason: Discretionary big-ticket purchase deferrable in recessions; cyclical residential homebuilder exposed to mortgage rates and housing cycle.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 2 (REJECT). National UK volume housebuilder. Residential home purchases are discretionary, deferrable big-ticket capital commitments highly sensitive to mortgage rates and general economic confidence. Cyclical homebuilders are explicitly excluded under Munger's non-deferrable everyday necessity standard.
qualitative.evidence: Bellway p.l.c. is a major UK housebuilder operating across England, Scotland, and Wales. Completions plunged 30% from 10,945 in FY23 to 7,654 in FY24 following the UK mortgage rate surge. Operating margins shrank from 16.0% in FY23 to ~10.0% in FY24, and pre-tax profit fell over 50% to £226M. While Bellway maintains a relatively conservative balance sheet with net cash (£10M-£50M) and disciplined land buying, its financial returns fluctuate wildly across the economic cycle (ROCE falling from >20% in 2021-2022 to <8% in 2024). It possesses no pricing power to counteract build-cost inflation or mortgage-driven buyer deferrals.
